notes:
Overview: Mid-market B2B SaaS (search + recommendation) evaluating Redwood for embeddings + semantic search. Initial interest started with Hosted API for quick integration, now moving to Dedicated because of throughput predictability and cost concerns.

Use case details:
- Primary: semantic search across product docs + customer conversations (~1M documents, mixed text and attachments).
- Secondary: embeddings for recommendations and reranking in discovery flows.
- Ingestion: nightly batch jobs (ETL) generating ~200k embeddings/day; peak reindex jobs of ~1M docs/month.
- Latency/throughput targets: embeddings API <100ms p50, p99 <300ms; search query throughput target 150 QPS sustained for peak windows.

POC history and results so far:
- 2-week Hosted API POC (Jan 25 - Feb 8): integrated SDK + async batch pipeline. Observed average embedding latency ~85ms, p95 ~240ms; cost higher than expected at scale.
- Bulk ingest test: 200k docs seeded via batch connector; saw throttling at 1.2k concurrent workers -> raised questions about auto-batching and backpressure behavior.
- Semantic search eval: reranking experiments with Redwood embeddings improved MRR by ~12% vs baseline TF-IDF.
- Engineering note: KV cache and prefix caching not applicable for batch embed workloads; need config guidance from Redwood Optimize.

Technical requirements called out by infra: 
- Vector DB: currently on Pinecone managed; evaluating tighter integration or direct vector store (self-hosted Milvus) behind VPC. Need reference architecture for Redwood + Pinecone + VPC egress.
- Batch jobs: need reliable bulk upload API and idempotency guarantees; asked for recommended rate limits and retry patterns.
- Data controls: SSO (SAML), audit logs, and KMS integration mandatory. Some customers require EU residency.

Commercial and ops notes:
- Started as self-serve sign-up (trial) -> AE outreach 2025-11-20.
- Pricing conversation: team asks for per-embedding effective unit costs vs Pinecone and a Dedicated reserved capacity quote (3-node baseline, monthly commit). See pricing deck in Drive.
- Quote sensitivity: procurement wants two scenarios: 12-month reserved vs pay-as-you-go burstable.

Recent activities (bulleted timeline):
- 2026-01-25: Kickoff call; scope embed POC (Jordan, Avery, SummitRidge Eng lead). Fireflies ff_2026-02-18_9432 recorded.
- 2026-02-12: Batch ingest test results shared; engineering asks for recommended batching knobs.
- 2026-02-18: Deep dive with SE (Avery) on vector DB topology + indexing strategies. Action: SE to provide arch diagram.
- 2026-02-25: Pricing deck (drive) shared by AE.
- 2026-03-02: Prod perf follow-up meeting; discussed Dedicated soak. Fireflies ff_2026-03-02_1119.
- 2026-03-09: Legal sent initial vendor questionnaire; flagged EU residency requirement for two enterprise customers.

Quotes/voice of customer: 
- "Hosted API is fast to get started but costs started to add up at scale — we need predictable unit economics." — Product lead
- "If we can hit sustained 150 QPS and keep embedding costs down, Dedicated makes sense." — VP Eng

Open action items and next steps:
- SE (Avery) to deliver Redwood + Pinecone VPC integration diagram and recommended rate-limit settings (by 2026-03-15).
- Engineering to approve Dedicated soak window: propose 72h perf soak on a 3-node Dedicated cluster (scheduled week of 2026-03-22).
- AE (Jordan) to send two pricing scenarios and DPA template to SummitRidge procurement.
- Legal/Procurement to review DPA/data residency response; blocker until EU residency path confirmed.

Blockers (short):
- Need clear throughput SLO commitments for Dedicated (p50/p95/p99).
- Vector DB integration topology and VPC egress details pending.
- Budget sign-off requires cost model comparing Redwood Dedicated vs current Pinecone + self-hosted infra.

Internal notes for Redwood: 
- Prioritize architecture doc for Hosted->Dedicated migration pattern and cost model for bulk embedding workloads.
- Flag for product: batch-embed idempotency and bulk-upload API could be product differentiators for mid-market SaaS.

Linked artifacts: pricing deck, POC test plan, vendor questionnaire (Drive links above), Fireflies recordings, support tickets RINF-3421 (batch failure analysis), RINF-3587 (rate-limit guidance).

Summary (one-liner): Strong mid-market prospect moving from Hosted POC to Dedicated evaluation driven by throughput predictability and cost at scale; legal/residency + vector DB integration are the immediate blockers.
